BiblicalUsage: Tammuz was a Phoenician god, and Ezekiel is brought to the door of the north gate of the Lord's house, where women sit weeping for Tammuz. The weeping was a yearly rite for a dying god of vegetation, mourned and hoped to return. It is named once, in the list of abominations shown to the prophet inside the temple itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the weeping for Tammuz is the saddest idolatry in Ezekiel: women mourning a god who dies every year, in the house of the God who lives for ever.
